heading: What each service language can use in the browser
body:
A service in Rust, Go, C#, F#, Kotlin, Java, Dart, Ruby, Lua, Swift, Python or C++ runs in the page, but it does not call the browser itself. It reaches the browser only through Tachyon: the view reads its fields and calls its methods, events carry values in and out, and the storage annotations keep its data. Tachyon also gives every language but Python and C++ a small set of browser APIs: `Clock`, `SecureRandom`, `Connectivity`, `PageVisibility`, `Preferences`, `Clipboard`, `Share`, `Notifications` and `Geolocation`. Every language but Lua, Python and C++ also gets `WindowControls` (see the next sections and the feature "What a page may do to its window"). Python and C++ services do not have these browser APIs yet: a Python browser API stops the build with `TY1605`, and a C++ `Needs` field may name only a C++ service or `HTTPClient` (`TY1372`). A Lua service has no `WindowControls` and no `FilePicker`: such a field in a Lua service stops the build with `TY2015`. Other browser work lives in a JavaScript or TypeScript service. That service publishes a typed event, and the service in the other language receives it with `OnEvent`.

The table shows what each language can use in the page.

| What | Rust | Go | C# | F# | Kotlin | Dart | Ruby | Lua | Swift | Java | Python | C++ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fields and methods for the view | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `publishEvent` and `OnEvent` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes, synchronous listeners | Yes |
| `Store` and caches | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No, not yet (ADR 0085) | Yes | Yes | No, not yet (`TY1308`) | No, not yet (`TY1308`) |
| `LocalState` and `SessionState` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No, not yet (ADR 0085) | Yes | Yes | No, not yet (`TY1308`) | No, not yet (`TY1308`) |
| `HTTPClient` sent by the browser | Yes, with `Needs` | Yes, with `Needs` | Yes, with `Needs` | Yes, with its own `BehaviorContext` | Yes, with `Needs` | Yes, with `Needs` | Yes, with `Needs` | No | Yes, with `Needs` | Yes, with `Needs` | No (`TY1308`) | Yes, with `Needs` |
| `HTTPClient` sent by the Setup's HTTP adapter, with `Cached`, `ClearCache` and `UpdateCache` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No, not yet (ADR 0085) | Yes | Yes | No (`TY1308`) | No, not yet (`TY1308`) |
| `StreamRequest` and `SocketRequest` | Yes, with `Needs`; messages arrive through `OnEvent` | Yes, with `Needs`; messages arrive through `OnEvent` | No | No | No | Yes, with `Needs`; messages arrive through `OnEvent` | No | No | No | No | No (`TY1605`) | No (`TY1308`) |
| `Clock` and `SecureRandom` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No, not yet (`TY1605`) | No, not yet (`TY1372`) |
| `Connectivity`, `PageVisibility`, `Preferences` and their change events | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No, not yet (`TY1605`) | No, not yet (`TY1372`) |
| `Clipboard`, `Share`, `Notifications` and `Geolocation`, after a grant | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No, not yet (`TY1605`) | No, not yet (`TY1372`) |
| `WindowControls`, after a grant in `tac.application.window.controls` (a native window only) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No (`TY2015`) | Yes | Yes | No | No, not yet (`TY1372`) |
| The current time from the language itself | No, use `Clock` | Yes | Yes | Yes, `System.DateTime.UtcNow` | Yes, `System.currentTimeMillis()` | Yes | Yes | No `os` library, use `Clock` | No `Date` (no Foundation), use `Clock` | Yes, `System.currentTimeMillis()` | Yes, `time.time()` | Not checked yet |
| Random numbers from the language itself | No, use `SecureRandom` | Yes | Yes | Yes, `System.Random` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes, `math.random` | Yes, `Int.random(in:)` | Yes, `java.util.Random` | Yes, `random` | Not checked yet |
| Wait (sleep) | No | Yes, the page waits | Yes, the page waits | Yes, `Thread.Sleep` makes the page wait | Yes, `Thread.sleep` makes the page wait | Yes, in an `async` method | No | No | Yes, `Task.sleep` in an `async` method makes the page wait | No; only the wait of a `Retry` or a blocking `MaxAtOnce`, which makes the page wait | No; `async def` stops the build (`TY1605`) | Not checked yet |
| Console output | No | Yes | Yes | Yes, `printfn` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes, `print` | Yes, `print` | Yes, `System.out` | Yes, `print` | Yes, `std::cout` |

A Swift, Rust, C# or Kotlin service that a native app links in has no page, but it can still get `WindowControls`: it declares an uninitialized `WindowControls` field with `Needs` or `NeedsAll`, and Tachyon calls the host directly, with the same grants (ADR 0089).

Send requests from a JavaScript, TypeScript, Dart, C#, F#, Rust, Go, Kotlin, Swift, Java, Ruby or C++ client (see "Calling the server from a page"). In Lua and Python, a JavaScript or TypeScript client sends them. Its answers, and the messages of a stream or a socket, reach the other languages as typed events. In Rust, `std::time::SystemTime::now()` and `std::thread::sleep` stop the service with an error, and `println!` prints nothing. Use Tachyon's `Clock` and `SecureRandom` instead (see "Clock and secure random numbers"). Ruby refuses `sleep`: a Ruby call waits only for a request to the server. The Lua runtime has no `io`, `os` or `package` library, so a Lua service reads the time from `Clock`.

Tachyon refuses code that calls the browser directly, and the build stops with `TY1317`: Go `syscall/js`; Dart `dart:js_interop`, `dart:js_interop_unsafe`, `dart:js`, `dart:js_util`, `dart:html`, `package:web` and `package:js`; C# and F# `System.Runtime.InteropServices.JavaScript`, `JSImport`, `JSExport` and `JSHost`; Rust `wasm_bindgen`, `web_sys`, `js_sys` and `wasm_import_module`; Kotlin `external`, `@JsFun`, `@JsExport`, `@JsModule`, `@JsName`, `js(…)`, `kotlinx.browser`, `org.w3c` and `kotlin.js`; Java `org.teavm`, `native` methods and TeaVM's `JS…` annotations such as `JSBody`, `JSObject` and `JSExport`; Ruby `TachyonWeb` and `JS`; and Swift `JavaScriptKit`, `JavaScriptEventLoop`, `JSObject`, `JSValue`, `JSClosure`, `JSPromise`, `@_extern` and `@_expose`. Such code breaks the test units of the language, and a native target has no browser. Tachyon's own code on the page is not checked.

Two smaller browser APIs exist only in some languages. `PreferenceStrings` reads and writes short texts in the browser's `localStorage` with `read(key)` and `write(key, value)`; JavaScript, TypeScript and Java services have it after the grant `preferenceStrings` in `tac.browserApis`, and a refused or failed call gives back `null` or `false`. `DocumentTitle` sets the title of the page with `set(title)`; JavaScript, TypeScript and Kotlin services have it.

In the example, `PlaceService` in JavaScript or TypeScript reads the browser and publishes a `PlaceFound` event. `MapService` receives the event with `OnEvent`, and the view shows its fields. Write `MapService` in any service language: the tabs show each one. A Python listener is a synchronous `@on_event` method. The same pattern works for any browser API outside Tachyon's set.
